About the experiment

The dataset records acoustic flame-extinguishing experiments across LPG, gasoline, thinner, and kerosene. The system uses sound generated by a speaker to disturb the flame and test whether the flame is extinguished under different experimental conditions.

Variables

FUEL identifies the fuel. DISTANCE is the separation between the acoustic source and flame. FREQUENCY is the tested acoustic frequency. DESIBEL is the recorded sound-pressure level. AIRFLOW records airflow associated with the experimental condition. SIZE is a device/flame-setting code. STATUS is the binary extinction outcome.

Important coding detail

SIZE should not be interpreted as a single continuous physical size scale. In particular, the LPG records use settings that correspond to throttle conditions, so the dashboard treats SIZE as categorical.

How to read this dashboard

Start with Overview to establish the experiment and the overall outcome. Use Experimental conditions to understand which settings are represented. Extinction relationships focuses on the outcome and interactions. Finally, use Variable explorer to investigate one explanatory variable at a time.

Analytical caution

The plots describe observed associations. They should not automatically be interpreted as causal effects. Several experimental variables are related to one another—for example, distance and airflow—so a strong one-variable relationship does not imply that the variable acts independently.

Source inspiration

This dashboard is a new implementation inspired by the structure and exploratory intent of the supplied Tableau dashboard, while using a different layout, interaction model, and analytical emphasis.

Dataset: Acoustic Extinguisher Fire Dataset. Values and summary statistics are calculated dynamically from the embedded workbook data.
